data.title: New GitLab Agentic Automations Clear the Security Backlog and Do Up to Twice the Work For The Same Cost
data.description:
All Remote - GitLab Inc., the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps, today announced GitLab 19.6, with new capabilities that help security teams work down vulnerability backlogs, make GitLab Credits go further, automate recurring tasks, and bring agents into Slack conversations where teams make decisions. These capabilities help organizations put agents to work across more of the software lifecycle while keeping visibility and control over agent activity and spending.

Engineering, security, and product teams now use agents for a wider range of tasks. As that use grows, organizations need the cost of agent work to stay manageable. They also need automation that lets agents move work forward without someone starting each task. GitLab 19.6 delivers both, with controls that show which agent acted, what it could access, and what it did.

Reducing Vulnerability Backlogs With Agentic Remediation

Every team is adding security findings faster than they can clear them. GitLab 19.6 extends agentic remediation so GitLab Duo security agents can work through more of that backlog. Security managers can turn on agent flows across many projects at once, and teams can run those flows on branches other than the default to fix findings before code merges.

A new vulnerability context flow, in beta for SAST findings, shows whether a flaw is exploitable in practice, so teams can prioritize by exploitability as well as severity. A new mean time to remediation chart shows whether remediation keeps pace with discovery, and group-level policies hold changes with critical or known-exploited vulnerabilities until a designated approver signs off.

When secret detection finds an active GitLab personal access token, teams can now rotate it and fix the code in one step. Rotate and fix, now in beta on GitLab.com, revokes the leaked token, creates a replacement with the same permissions, and stores it in GitLab Secrets Manager. GitLab Duo then opens a merge request that removes the hardcoded token from the code.

Scheduling Recurring Agent Tasks

Recurring tasks such as issue triage wait on a person or an event to start them, so teams complete them late or not at all. Scheduled automations, now in beta, run GitLab Duo Agent Platform flows in the background on a set cadence, from every 15 minutes to every three months. A team can triage new issues daily, or check CI health every hour and post the likely root cause before anyone starts investigating.

Each automation runs as a dedicated service account with scoped permissions, so audit events separate agent activity from human activity and record every change. A redesigned Automations page shows what ran, how often it succeeded, and why a run failed. These controls make scheduled automations a building block of the governed software factory.

Bringing Agents Into Slack Conversations

Software decisions often start in Slack, and someone then retypes them into GitLab. GitLab for Slack lets teams mention @GitLab in a thread or direct message to turn those decisions into issues, merge requests, and agent flows. The agent posts results back to the thread.

Each request runs with the requester's own GitLab permissions, creates an agent session in GitLab, and draws from GitLab Credits. Merge requests follow the same reviews, approvals, and audit trail as any other change.

GitLab for Slack is now generally available on GitLab.com for Premium and Ultimate customers, and GitLab plans to add support for GitLab Self-Managed next month.

Each GitLab Credit Now Does Up to Twice the Work

GitLab has made agentic usage on GitLab Duo Agent Platform more efficient and is passing those savings on to customers. Each task given to Duo Agent Platform now results in fewer model requests, such that most customers will see their GitLab Credits go up to twice as far.

Organizations can use the freed-up credits for the new agentic remediation and scheduled automations, and to extend agentic work to Slack. Customers who have Flex contracts can also use available credits for recently introduced innovations such as GitLab Secrets Manager, Dedicated Hosted Runners, and coming soon, GitLab Orbit. This builds on recent tools for managing credit spend, including impact and cost analytics to track usage and manage credit caps.

The change takes effect on November 19, 2026, for new customers. Existing customers move to it on December 18 or can opt in earlier.

GitLab 19.6 also includes the following updates:

  • MCP governance. With new controls now in beta, group owners can set each GitLab MCP server tool to Always Allow, Always Ask, or Always Deny, and every tool call through the MCP server now creates an audit event. Security teams control what agents can do in GitLab and keep a record of everything they did.

  • GitLab Duo flows from the tools developers already use. When Claude Code, Cursor, or another MCP client connects, the GitLab MCP server suggests a matching GitLab Duo flow and confirms before starting it. Developers hand work to GitLab agents without switching tools.

  • Rapid Diffs. A rebuilt merge request view, now generally available, loads the first file about three times faster. Reviews start in seconds, even on large merge requests.

  • Resumable jobs and auto-merge time windows. Agent sessions can pause and resume where they left off, and teams can set a time window for auto-merge. Long-running agent work doesn't have to start over, and changes merge only when the team is ready.

To learn more about the 19.6 release, please read the what's new page. Teams can also find guidance on building and scaling with agents in the AI-Native Engineering Playbook and GitLab Well Architected guide.

Supporting Quotes

  • “Teams make decisions in Slack every day, and the best agents are the ones that can act on that context,” said Katie Steigman, vice president product management, Slack. “GitLab for Slack lets agents read the conversation, take action across the software lifecycle in GitLab, and bring the results back to the thread. Teams can go from a quick discussion to planned, reviewed, and shipped work without switching tools.”

  • “Every organization is racing to keep up with the security challenges that have become the new norm,” said Manav Khurana, chief product and marketing officer, GitLab. “GitLab 19.6 helps security teams clear vulnerability backlogs faster, and provides new automations. Both of which are easier to afford now that each GitLab Credit can be used for more agentic work.”

About GitLab

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 70 million registered users and approximately 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

data.title: Hyperfine to Present at the Piper Sandler 38th Annual Healthcare Conference on December 3

Hyperfine, Inc. (), the groundbreaking health technology company that has redefined brain imaging with the first FDA-cleared AI-powered portable MRI system for the brain—the Swoop® system—today announced that management will present at the Piper Sandler 38th Annual Healthcare Conference in New York on Thursday, December 3, 2026 at 9:10 a.m. Eastern Time. A live webcast, as well as an archived recording, will be available on the “Investors” section of the Company’s website at: https://investors.hyperfine.io/. The webcast will be archived and available for replay for at least 90 days after the event.

The Swoop® Portable MR Imaging® Systems are U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared for brain imaging of patients of all ages. They are portable, ultra-low-field magnetic resonance imaging devices for producing images that display the internal structure of the head where full diagnostic examination is not clinically practical. When interpreted by a trained physician, these images provide information that can be useful in determining a diagnosis.

About Hyperfine, Inc.

Hyperfine, Inc. () is the groundbreaking health technology company that has redefined brain imaging with the Swoop® system—the first FDA-cleared, portable, ultra-low-field, magnetic resonance brain imaging system capable of providing imaging at multiple points of professional care. Founded by Dr. Jonathan Rothberg in a technology-based incubator called 4Catalyzer, Hyperfine, Inc. scientists, engineers, and physicists developed the Swoop® system out of a passion for redefining brain imaging methodology and how clinicians can apply accessible diagnostic imaging to patient care. data.title: Gold Reserve Announces Intention to Make Final Offers to Settle CVR and Bonus Entitlements
data.description:
Gold Reserve Ltd. (TSX.V: GRZ) (BSX: GRZ.BH) () (“Gold Reserve” or the “Company”) announced today that it intends to make final offers to holders of its outstanding contingent value rights (“CVRs”) and to participants in its 2012 bonus plan (“Bonus Plan”) to settle all or a portion of their respective entitlements in exchange for a cash payment. The Company previously reported its intention to make such offers in August 2026.

The proposed settlement offers are expected to be made on substantially the same terms as the settlement offers previously made by the Company to CVR holders and Bonus Plan participants earlier in 2026. The proposed settlement offers are expected to remain open for a limited period and to expire in early December 2026, on a specific date to be determined by the Company and communicated to the applicable CVR holders and Bonus Plan participants.

Further details regarding the proposed settlement offers, including the applicable terms and expiry date, will be communicated directly to CVR holders and Bonus Plan participants in due course.

The Company also provided an update in respect to its previously announced intention to offer holders of options expiring in February 2027 the opportunity to surrender their options in exchange for a cash payment at a discount to the market price. Following further consideration, management has determined not to proceed with the proposed offer at this time; however, management may consider offers at a later date. Holders of outstanding options retain the ability to exercise their options, including through cashless and net exercise, in accordance with the terms of the Company’s amended equity incentive plan.

About Gold Reserve

Gold Reserve is a primarily US-owned mineral exploration and development company, domiciled in Bermuda, focused on advancing high-quality mineral assets with the objective of creating sustainable long-term value for shareholders. The Company is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (TSX-V: GRZ), the Bermuda Stock Exchange (BSX: GRZ.BH), and trades in the United States on the OTCQX ().

data.title: Curtiss-Wright Announces $250 Million Expansion of 2026 Share Repurchase Program and Declares Dividend of $0.26 Per Share for Common Stock
data.description:
Curtiss-Wright Corporation () today announced a $250 million expansion of its 2026 share repurchase program, which is now expected to result in record annual share repurchases of $710 million in 2026. The Board of Directors has also declared a quarterly dividend of twenty-six cents ($0.26) per share of its Common Stock, payable December 11, 2026, to stockholders of record as of November 27, 2026.

“We are pleased to announce another $250 million expansion of our 2026 repurchase program, as we remain on track to deliver record financial performance and record share repurchases this year,” said Lynn M. Bamford, Chair and CEO of Curtiss-Wright Corporation. “Share repurchase remains a key element of our disciplined capital allocation strategy, underscoring our Board of Directors’ continued confidence in Curtiss-Wright’s Pivot to Growth strategy, healthy balance sheet and strong financial outlook, and our commitment to delivering sustainable long-term value to shareholders.”

This program will be conducted in concurrence with the existing $60 million share repurchase program being executed this year and follows the completion of $400 million in opportunistic programs that were executed earlier in 2026.

In addition, the Board of Directors authorized repurchases, beginning in January 2027, of $60 million in shares via a 10b5-1 program, which is expected to offset potential dilution from compensation plans. Entering 2027, the Company will have remaining open authorization of $290 million.

About Curtiss-Wright Corporation

Curtiss-Wright Corporation () is a global integrated business that provides highly engineered products, solutions and services mainly to Aerospace & Defense markets, as well as critical technologies in demanding Commercial Nuclear Power, Process and Industrial markets. We leverage a workforce of approximately 9,300 highly skilled employees who develop, design and build what we believe are the best engineered solutions to the markets we serve. Building on the heritage of Glenn Curtiss and the Wright brothers, Curtiss-Wright has a long tradition of providing innovative solutions through trusted customer relationships. data.title: US yields fall as a drop in equities drives safe-haven buying in bonds
data.description:
Key points:
  • US stocks drop even as Anthropic shares rise in debut
  • JPMorgan sees quarter-point rate hikes in January, March
  • Auction of 10-year TIPS shows solid demand

By Caroline Valetkevitch

US Treasury yields eased on Thursday as a sharp selloff in US equities pushed investors to buy safe-haven bonds.

Anthropic's market debut, which was the largest IPO on record, failed to revive faded enthusiasm over AI. All three of the major US stock indexes were more than 2% lower even as Anthropic's shares climbed.

Investors are worried about the future of the AI buildout, which has been a boost to the economy. AI leader Nvidia's stock has been under pressure as the company's CEO resigned last week after reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected by US intelligence of being ​a Chinese spy.

"It's a flight to quality. The stock market just is not looking very robust," said Tom di Galoma, managing director at Mischler Financial Group in Stamford, Connecticut. "For the most part, clients are putting money to work in fixed income, especially in the long end."

If the economic outlook is weakening, di Galoma said, the Federal Reserve is not likely to raise interest rates by more than 25 basis points in December.

Bond prices rise as yields fall. Yields were slightly higher earlier in the day, with investors focusing on the rate hike outlook.

The Fed is widely expected to raise interest rates in December after leaving rates unchanged in October. It hiked rates in September for the first time in three years in an effort to combat inflation.

Traders have been factoring in more rate hikes in the coming months, especially after data last week showed consumer prices rose more quickly than expected in October.

Fed funds futures traders on Thursday were pricing in about a 96% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the US central bank's December 8-9 meeting, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool, and just a 4% chance of a 50-basis-point hike.

Among recent hawkish comments, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said on CNBC on Wednesday that the central bank needs to get more aggressive in its response to inflation.

J.P. Morgan said earlier on Thursday it expects the Fed to deliver quarter-point rate hikes in January and March next year, on top of a previously forecast December increase.

Also on Thursday, the auction of 10-year TIPS showed solid demand, reflecting investor appetite for locking in attractive real yields of nearly 3% while retaining protection against potential inflation surprises. The US 10-year TIPS yield (US10YTIP=RR) extended its fall after the auction.

Earlier, investors digested economic data showing the number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits increased slightly last week.

The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note was down 2.2 basis points at 5.044%. The yield on the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) was down 1.3 basis points at 5.399%.

A closely watched part of the US Treasury yield curve measuring the gap between yields on 2- and 10-year Treasury notes (US2US10=TWEB), seen as an indicator of economic expectations, was at a positive 28.0 basis points.

The 2-year (US2YT=RR) US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, was down 4 basis points at 4.76%.

The breakeven rate on 5-year US Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) (US5YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.220% after closing at 2.231% on Wednesday.

The 10-year TIPS breakeven rate (US10YTIP=TWEB) was last at 2.185%, indicating the market sees inflation averaging about 2.2% a year for the next decade.
